doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Learning chords from Winn books
summary: Learned from sheet music, then discovered chord symbols via books his father brought; began to see music as a living.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: And how did you learn “Sweet Lorraine?” From sheet music?

Sheet music. Originally sheet music and sheet music had the chord symbols and the melody and all that accompaniment and I played with the accompaniment and all, but I never knew what those figures were up above. Nobody ever told me. I had no theory. Never had theory in my life. And finally one day my dad came home, my dad again, he came home with a bunch of books. The Winn books W-I-N-N, How to Play Ragtime, How to Play Breaks and Endings and all that sort of different things. And in the back of the book there were chords with the notes on them. And I said aha, that’s what this C seven means. And I wound up that I would write in little things in the sheet music, in pencil, and write in little fills and then I’d apply them to different chords and different situations until I had them memorized where I could just play it. And the light bulb went off. And I felt really great about it.

Yeah. It was really good. It opened up a whole world for me. And about that time I said hey, this is a way to make a living possibly. I started getting wedding jobs and wedding jobs didn’t pay very much, it paid anywhere from twelve to fifteen dollars for the night. But in those days it wasn’t too bad. Those days. Sounds like the Middle Ages.
